status: proposed schema, to be fixed with the coordinator before any training; nothing trained, nothing scored, no image read
task: Subject-held-out, session-matched check on NUAA with LivenessNet (coordinator, C2 card, 3 November 2026): four subject folds, three training seeds, counts per class and session, fitting/dev/test separation and budget, fixed before the training. Diagnostic design, not a benchmark and not a complete causal isolation: it mixes the three sessions in training and does not preserve the official NUAA protocol. Exploratory: the NUAA session-03 results of C1, M1, N1 and N2 are already known; every choice below is a rule fixed before any training, none is chosen on a result.
question: When the capture session is represented in training, does the N1 recipe generalise to subjects it has never seen? N2 already measured the opposite cell (the 9 training subjects in session 03: BPCER 0.6873 for every seed, AUROC 0.3171-0.4569); this schema measures new subjects with every session represented in training.
manifests_source: M2 package 20261006-M2-seed42-36c677a (accepted); the manifests are restricted; their SHA-256 and counts are those recorded in the accepted N1 and N2 configurations

expected.note: official lists: 3,491 + 9,123 images of 16 subjects (9 with sessions 01-02, 16 in session 03); cache nuaa_1500.npz = cnn_train + cnn_es + cnn_test

unit: subject (the independent unit of NUAA: the frames of one subject in one session are correlated, consecutive frames of one capture, M2)

strata_definition.A: frames in sessions 01-02 and bona fide frames in session 03
strata_definition.B: frames in sessions 01-02, no bona fide frame in session 03
strata_definition.C: no frame in sessions 01-02, bona fide frames in session 03
strata_definition.D: no frame in sessions 01-02, no bona fide frame in session 03

folds.dealing: balanced: subjects in stratum order A, B, C, D and ascending identifier, each to the fold with the fewest subjects, ties to the fold with the fewest subjects sharing a property (frames in sessions 01-02 for A and B, bona fide in session 03 for A and C, both counts for A), then the lowest index
folds.dealing_text: one subject at a time, in stratum order A, B, C, D and ascending identifier, to the fold with the fewest subjects; ties go to the fold with the fewest subjects sharing a property with the subject (frames in sessions 01-02 for A and B, bona fide frames in session 03 for A and C, the sum of the two counts for A), then to the lowest fold index; no random number
folds.constraints: every fold must hold at least two subjects with bona fide frames in session 03, two with attack frames in session 03 and two with frames in sessions 01-02 (so no test or dev stratum rests on one subject); otherwise FAIL, no fallback
folds.dev_fold: fold (k mod K) + 1 for the held-out fold k
folds.roles_text: for the held-out fold k: test = the subjects of fold k (all their frames, every session); dev = the subjects of fold k mod K + 1 (early stopping, learning-rate schedule, checkpoint restore and the EER threshold); fitting = the subjects of the other two folds; the three roles are disjoint by subject, so no subject of the test fold is ever seen in fitting or dev
folds.members: restricted output fold_members.csv (subject identifiers are never public); its SHA-256 is in the public schema

sampling.rule: spread(sorted file names of the cell, n): one every len/n, from the first
sampling.test: all frames of the held-out subjects
sampling.text: fitting: 350 frames per cell (class x session, 6 cells, 2,100 frames) of the fitting subjects, dev: 100 frames per cell (600 frames) of the dev subjects, both taken with the deterministic spread rule of M2 and train_cnn.py over the file names of the cell sorted ascending; a cell with fewer frames than required is FAIL; test: every frame of the held-out subjects, reported per session stratum (NA where a class is absent)
sampling.why_fixed_counts: equal weight of the three sessions in fitting (the session is the factor under study), fitting size close to N1 (2,507 frames), dev size close to N1 (493 frames); the counts are the largest multiples of 50 below the smallest availability over the four held-out folds (fitting: 361 bona fide frames of session 02 for held-out fold 3, so 350; dev: 117 bona fide frames of session 02 for held-out fold 1, so 100); in session 03 the fixed counts use a minority of the available frames (about 18-25% of the bona fide and 11-13% of the attacks), in sessions 01-02 most of them (about 69-97%): declared in the limits

frames.cache: frames whose key is in cnn_train, cnn_es or cnn_test are read from the training cache nuaa_1500.npz (SHA-256 dc286dc371e61d638da1842c062a38c5368a9ec4da07ccbc36b7fff6f3177920), reproduced bit for bit from the originals in N2
frames.to_extract: the other frames are extracted from the originals with the frozen cache extractor face.py of commit 0ac7143 (SHA-256 c72f7fa8a9f3b099babce2255530466e5a34731fb5d021f97fd412a98cb58261, delivered with N2) and the unchanged chain of train_cnn.preprocess (RetinaFace, Haar fallback, whole frame without a face; square crop margin 0.15; 256x256 INTER_AREA; BGR to RGB; reference enhancement; uint8), with the N2 cache check (every cache frame reproduced bit for bit) repeated before the extraction
frames.detector_per_frame: recorded (RetinaFace, Haar, none) for every extracted frame, restricted

architecture: LivenessNet (src/architectures.py of the coordinator's liveness-detection repository, the architecture used in C1 and N1), chosen by the coordinator on 3 November 2026 to stay comparable with N1

training.checkpoint: weights of the epoch with minimum val_loss on the dev frames (EarlyStopping restore_best_weights; set_weights when the epochs end first)
training.loss: CategoricalCrossentropy, one-hot labels (index 0 bona fide, 1 attack)
training.class_weight: balanced on the fitting set: n / (2 * n_class)
training.augmentation: RandomFlip(horizontal), RandomRotation(0.03), RandomZoom(0.12, 0.12), RandomTranslation(0.06, 0.06), RandomBrightness(0.15, value_range=(0, 1)), RandomContrast(0.2), GaussianNoise(0.02); fitting set only
training.seeds: train_seed for random, numpy and TensorFlow (weight initialisation, augmentation, batch order); no split seed: the folds and the samples are deterministic
training.device: CPU (training and scoring; the Metal GPU defect of N1)
training.trainings: K folds x 3 seeds = 12, one checkpoint each; weights restricted, cards and SHA-256 delivered

threshold.criterion: eer, the M1 protocol: candidates = distinct dev scores plus nextafter(min, -inf) if >= 0; attack if score > value (tie = bona fide); minimum of |fp * n_attack - fn * n_bona_fide| on integers, ties to the highest value
threshold.frozen_before_test: written from the dev scores before any test scoring; SHA-256 recorded; applied unchanged
threshold.also_reported: the fixed threshold 0.5 of C1, N1 and N2, labelled
threshold.dev_reuse_declared: the dev frames drive early stopping, learning-rate reduction, the restored epoch and the threshold (as in N1 and in the C2 protocol); the dev does not identify a unique threshold when its classes separate completely (M1) and gives no guarantee of transfer

metrics.per_unit: per fold, seed and session stratum of the held-out subjects (01, 02, 03 and all), NA where a class is absent: n_bona_fide, n_attack, accepted attacks, rejected bona fide, APCER, BPCER, ACER at 0.5 and at the dev threshold, AUROC (threshold-free)
metrics.aggregation: values of every fold and seed; median and range over seeds per fold; pooled counts over the four folds per session (every subject held out exactly once, so the pooled session-03 test covers the 16 subjects); no fold or seed selection
metrics.uncertainty: bootstrap over subjects: 1,000 resamples with replacement of the 16 held-out subjects (pooled over the four folds, per seed), percentile 2.5-97.5 of the pooled ACER and AUROC per session; random seed 0, fixed here; no statistical test. Declared: the pooled estimate is a cross-validation aggregate scored by four models with four dev thresholds; the session strata hold at most 9 subjects (sessions 01-02: 9; session 03 bona fide: 9), so the interval is coarse; no interval for a stratum with fewer than 5 subjects
metrics.pre_commitment: reported whatever the outcome; no change of recipe, threshold criterion, folds or counts after any score is read

budget.estimate: about 8-11 min per training on the CPU for 2,507 fitting frames in N1 (wall 496-671 s); 2,100 fitting frames here, so at most about 2.5 h of training; extraction of the frames outside the cache with the frozen extractor, once, before the trainings (the N2 cache check of 6,000 frames and the extraction of 491 ran in minutes); scoring of every frame of the held-out subjects, 12 passes; wall-time cap 6 h, else stop, no result, reported as a failed run
budget.on_cap_exceeded: stop, no results; report as a failed run

declarations.no_training_here: this package derives the schema only: no training, no inference, no image read, no face detection
declarations.diagnostic: diagnostic protocol, not a benchmark and not a complete causal isolation: adding session 03 to training also adds variety, so a low error on the held-out subjects would be consistent with an N1/C1 failure due to 'session not represented, or training data too narrow' rather than to the session alone; a high error would be consistent with a failure of the recipe; both readings are diagnostic, not causal
declarations.exploratory: the NUAA session-03 results are already known (C1, M1, N1, N2): the schema is a rule fixed before any training, not a confirmatory test
declarations.limits: frames of one subject and session stay correlated; per-subject counts are unbalanced (session 03 bona fide for 9 of 16 subjects, 3 of them training subjects); sessions 01-02 exist for 9 subjects only, so the session 01-02 test and dev strata rest on 2-3 subjects per fold and a single session x class cell there can rest on one subject (two training subjects lack bona fide frames in one of the two sessions); the fixed fitting counts under-sample session 03 (about 18-25% of its bona fide and 11-13% of its attacks are used) and use most of sessions 01-02; the dev of a held-out fold is the test fold of the next one, so the four fold results are not independent (different models, no leakage); three seeds give a range, not a confidence interval; one dataset, one attack type (print)
declarations.public_restricted: public: rules, counts per fold, role, session and class, SHA-256 of the restricted lists, budget; restricted: fold members, per-subject counts, the twelve per-fold manifests with keys and SHA-256
